name: Minimap2 in Codon (CSC 427)
summary: A reimplementation of Minimap2's core features in Python compiled with Codon, written for a CSC 427 student project and aiming to be more readable than the original C. Thirteen .codon files hold the sketching, indexing and utility layers, with 24 Seq plugin imports spread across twelve of them -- the widest per-file Seq usage in the index.
why_codon: README states the project implements Minimap2 in Python compiled with Codon, for readability over the C original.

name: scalce_codon
summary: A reimplementation of the SCALCE FASTQ compression algorithm in Codon, run through the Seq plugin. Four .codon files carry the Aho-Corasick trie, the pattern set and the compression and decompression paths.
why_codon: README states it is a reimplementation of SCALCE in Codon and gives the codon run -plugin seq invocation.

name: md5-codon
summary: An MD5 implementation in Codon that publishes its own measurements: 1.5x to 2.0x faster than hashlib.md5 and 1.1x to 1.2x faster than a Codon-plus-Python implementation. Three .codon files hold the digest, a test harness and a Codon-Python comparison, with ten inline LLVM sites across two of them.
why_codon: README reports the speedups directly against hashlib.md5 and against a Codon-plus-Python implementation.

name: strings.codon
summary: A Codon reimplementation of the Unix strings utility, one file, with seven C entry points bound for the file and memory handling.
why_codon: README is the title only. Inferred from the repo being a single-purpose Codon port of a Unix utility that the aim is a native-speed reimplementation.

name: xxd.codon
summary: A Codon reimplementation of the Unix xxd hex-dump utility, one file, no README, no Codon-specific feature used.
why_codon: No README. Inferred from the single-purpose Codon port of a Unix utility, matching the same author's strings.codon and md5-codon.

name: DS Tools
summary: Small helper binaries for pre- and post-processing datasets, split into combine_csv and split_csv with their own argument handling. The README says plainly that the tools are written in Codon just out of fun, and calls the language experimental.
why_codon: README states the tools are written in the experimental language Codon just out of fun; no performance claim is made.

name: pyext
summary: A worked example of packaging Codon as a Python extension module, driven by setup.py build_ext with a single .codon source and a Python test that exercises the compiled result through the Codon jit path.
why_codon: README gives the Codon install and build_ext steps. Inferred from the setup.py extension build that the point is demonstrating Codon-to-Python packaging.

name: r-packages-archives (codontest)
summary: An archive of R package experiments, one of which calls Codon from R. Two .codon files under codontest use the @export decorator to expose functions across the C boundary, taking a null-terminated string in from C and returning NumPy-shaped results. The only R-side Codon use found in the index.
why_codon: README is a bare title. Inferred from the codontest package structure and the @export functions taking C strings that Codon is being trialled as a native backend for an R package.

name: phaseProject
summary: A rudimentary simulation of a phase transition with pygame visualization. One .codon file holds the simulation, reaching pygame and the rest of the visualization stack through eight Python interop imports -- the densest use of Python interop per file in the index.
why_codon: README describes the simulation without naming Codon. Inferred from the single Codon source driving a pygame loop through Python interop that Codon supplies the simulation speed while Python supplies the graphics.

name: tmp.hack-llm-models
summary: A working copy around llama2.py, the pure-Python Llama 2 inference port. The single .codon file reimplements struct.unpack for reading model weights, since the Python struct module is not available under Codon.
why_codon: README is llama2.py's own. Inferred from a hand-written struct.unpack replacement that Codon was being tried as an accelerator for the inference loop and needed a missing stdlib piece supplied.

name: HCC Conda Recipes
summary: Conda build recipes maintained by the Holland Computing Center. One of them packages Seq 0.11.3 for cluster users, and the seven-line fib.codon is the recipe's build smoke test. Packaging rather than use, and evidence that Seq reached HPC software stacks.
why_codon: No Codon claim; the recipe packages Seq. Inferred from the recipe layout that fib.codon exists to verify the packaged compiler runs.

name: PL-ultimate-llm
summary: A loop in which a randomly chosen language model picks a real programming language and writes a real program in it, each result committed under a content-addressed directory. Codon came up as one of the chosen languages and the resulting eighteen-line Fibonacci program is stored under languages/Codon. The Codon here is model output, not human-authored.
why_codon: README describes the LLM loop. Inferred that Codon's presence reflects a model's language choice rather than any decision about Codon.
note: Machine-authored Codon: a language model chose the language at random and wrote the program. Flagged per ruling 6, kept as an ordinary entry.
